title: AMD silently removes memory encryption from consumer Ryzen CPUs
summary: AMD quietly removed TSME (Transparent Secure Memory Encryption) from consumer Ryzen CPUs through AGESA firmware updates, leaving users potentially vulnerable without notification. When journalists pressed AMD engineers for explanation, they went silent, raising concerns about corporate transparency on security matters.
problem_solved: Exposes a critical security regression where AMD removed transparent memory encryption from consumer CPUs without user awareness or clear explanation.
why_valuable: Highlights the importance of transparency in hardware security and alerts consumers about a potential vulnerability in their systems that they may be unaware of.
